title: Provision-to-Ready Baseline Metrics (Pre-Sprint) — Dedicated & Shared GPU Fleet
content:
Last updated: 2025-10-07 (data pull window: 2025-09-01 → 2025-09-28)
Owner: Jamal Pierce (Infra/Fleet)
Purpose: Baseline “time-to-ready” before Provision-to-Ready Automation sprint. Used to set SLO targets and measure improvement.

Definitions / methodology
- Population: GPU worker nodes provisioned for Dedicated pools and shared capacity expansions (excluding planned maintenance drains).
- “Allocated_at”: timestamp when capacity request is fulfilled and instance is assigned to a pool (currently: FleetOps allocation log / Terraform apply completion; see open question below).
- “Ready_at”: timestamp when node is actually usable for inference workloads.
  - Pre-sprint reality: not a single authoritative signal. We approximated Ready_at as: kubelet Ready + node labeled “serving=true” + manual operator confirmation in #eng-infra (when present).
- Time-to-ready = Ready_at - Allocated_at.
- Units: minutes unless noted.
- Notes:
  - Some nodes “appear” fast to kubelet Ready but were not truly usable (driver mismatch, NCCL flake) and required manual reimage; these show up as long tail due to rework.
  - We did not yet have per-step spans; step breakdown below is based on sampled logs (N=~25 per bucket) + operator notes.

Open questions (tracking in Slack thread)
- Source-of-truth for Allocated_at: Terraform apply end vs. EC2 instance running vs. capacity scheduler assignment? (Slack: eng-infra/1738791123)
- Source-of-truth for Ready_at: should become Fleet Readiness Service “READY” state once implemented.

====================
TAB 1 — Summary (All regions, all GPU types)
====================

Overall baseline (Sep 2025)
| Metric | Dedicated pools | Shared capacity | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Nodes provisioned (N) | 312 | 184 | Approx; from ops logs + cloud inventory |
| Time-to-ready P50 | 64 | 49 | Minutes |
| Time-to-ready P95 | 212 | 165 | Long tail mostly due to reimage + validation debugging |
| Time-to-ready P99 | 398 | 312 | Includes a few “stuck validating” / driver drift cases |
| Success without manual touch | 62% | 71% | Manual touch = any human action beyond initiating runbook |
| Reimage rate (any reason) | 18% | 11% | Pre-sprint (no gating) |
| Quarantine rate | 0% | 0% | No formal quarantine state pre-sprint |

Manual touch distribution (Dedicated pools)
| Manual touches per node | Share of nodes | Typical reasons |
|---:|---:|---|
| 0 | 62% | Clean bring-up |
| 1 | 24% | Label fix, restart kubelet, rerun ad-hoc GPU checks |
| 2 | 10% | Reimage once + join retry |
| 3+ | 4% | Reimage loop, driver/CUDA mismatch, NCCL fabric issues |

====================
TAB 2 — Time-to-ready by Region x GPU Type (Dedicated pools)
====================

| Region | GPU type | N | P50 | P75 | P95 | P99 | Success w/o manual touch | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| us-east-1 | A100-80GB | 148 | 58 | 84 | 188 | 322 | 66% | Best sampled data; primary expansion region |
| us-east-1 | H100-80GB | 22 | 76 | 112 | 246 | 410 | 55% | Higher variance; driver/CUDA matrix churn |
| us-west-2 | A100-80GB | 46 | 71 | 103 | 228 | 367 | 60% | More networking-related join delays |
| us-west-2 | L40S | 19 | 63 | 97 | 201 | 301 | 63% | Occasional containerd config drift |
| eu-central-1 | A100-80GB | 28 | 92 | 138 | 291 | 415 | 46% | Slowest; image pulls + CNI readiness delays |
| eu-central-1 | H100-80GB | 9 | 101 | 155 | 338 | 338 | 44% | Small N; a few “retry until works” cases |

Footnotes:
- “Success w/o manual touch” includes nodes that passed kubelet Ready and entered serving without operator action; pre-sprint this is fuzzy because serving label sometimes applied manually.
- P99 shown when N supports it; otherwise P99 ~ P95.

====================
TAB 3 — Time-to-ready by Region x GPU Type (Shared capacity)
====================

| Region | GPU type | N | P50 | P75 | P95 | Success w/o manual touch | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| us-east-1 | A100-80GB | 96 | 44 | 68 | 142 | 74% | Shared is less strict; fewer post-provision checks |
| us-west-2 | A100-80GB | 41 | 52 | 81 | 170 | 70% | Join delays during peak hours |
| us-east-1 | L40S | 29 | 46 | 73 | 156 | 72% | Some disk warmup variance |
| eu-central-1 | A100-80GB | 18 | 69 | 111 | 239 | 56% | Similar CNI + image pull issues |

====================
TAB 4 — Step-level breakdown (sampled) + where time is spent
====================

Important: We do not have instrumented spans yet. These are approximations based on:
- cloud-init timestamps
- kubelet logs
- operator notes (FleetOps checklist)
Sample size: ~25 nodes per bucket (us-east A100 Dedicated), smaller for others.

Step breakdown (Dedicated, us-east-1, A100-80GB) — minutes
| Step | P50 | P90 | P95 | Owner (today) | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| Allocate instance (capacity assigned) → EC2 running | 6 | 14 | 22 | FleetOps | Capacity contention increases P95 |
| Boot + cloud-init | 12 | 24 | 35 | FleetOps | Some variance due to package repos |
| Image pulls (base containers) | 8 | 28 | 42 | Infra | Spikes when cache miss + registry latency |
| NVIDIA driver/toolkit verification | 5 | 18 | 31 | Infra | Failures drive reimage loop |
| Kubelet join + node Ready | 11 | 27 | 48 | Infra/SRE | CNI readiness is frequent culprit |
| Post-provision ad-hoc validations (GPU health, NCCL) | 9 | 37 | 58 | Infra | Not standardized; often manual |
| Manual ops / rework time (if needed) | 0 | 96 | 182 | FleetOps | Dominates long tail |

Observed “rework” patterns
- Reimage once: adds ~45–120 min depending on queue + image pull.
- Reimage loop (2+): adds 150–300+ min; often due to inconsistent image versions + driver mismatch.
- “Validating stuck” (no formal state): adds 60–240 min due to unclear ownership (Infra vs Platform) and missing failure reasons.

====================
TAB 5 — Top delay contributors (ranked) + frequency
====================

Dedicated pools — primary delay drivers (Sep 2025)
| Rank | Delay contributor | Est. frequency among delayed nodes | Typical symptom | Typical remediation | Notes |
|---:|---|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | Driver/CUDA mismatch vs expected runtime | ~28% | nvidia-smi OK but runtime fails / wrong CUDA minor | Reimage; pin driver; manual package cleanup | See “driver matrix working notes” doc |
| 2 | Kubelet join / CNI readiness delays | ~21% | Node Ready flaps; CNI not ready; DNS issues | Restart kubelet; cordon/drain; check CNI logs | More common in eu-central |
| 3 | Image pull latency / registry throttling | ~17% | Long waits pulling base images | Retry pulls; pre-pull; warm cache | Shows as “fast boot but slow readiness” |
| 4 | NCCL smoke instability / fabric issues | ~12% | NCCL all-reduce timeout / hangs | Retry; adjust timeout; sometimes quarantine (informal) | No standardized canary pre-sprint |
| 5 | Disk warmup / ephemeral volume variance | ~9% | Slow container start; IO wait spikes | Reboot; replace instance | Common in L40S pool |
| 6 | Operator handoffs / unclear ownership | ~8% | Node “looks fine” but not serving; waiting on approvals | Slack pings; manual label updates | Should reduce with readiness service |
| 7 | Cluster-specific config drift | ~5% | containerd/kubelet flags differ by pool | Manual config fix; reimage | Motivates baseline config standard |

====================
TAB 6 — Notes by region (qualitative)
====================

us-east-1
- Generally most reliable and fastest. Biggest issue: driver/toolkit drift during upgrades and lack of a “golden image channel” process.
- Dedicated expansions often happen during business hours → contention on allocation + operator queues.

us-west-2
- Higher kubelet join variance; we suspect network policy/CNI rollout timing differences.
- Some “works after restart” cases: expensive in long tail.

eu-central-1
- Consistently slowest; frequent image pulls + CNI readiness delays.
- Smaller operator coverage window sometimes increases “time waiting for human” component.

====================
TAB 7 — Pre-sprint baseline takeaways (for sprint goal-setting)
====================

1) The median time-to-ready is acceptable-ish (~60 min Dedicated), but the P95 (~3.5 hours) is the problem customers feel during expansions.
2) Long tail is dominated by:
   - Reimage loops due to image/driver drift
   - Networking/kubelet join uncertainty
   - Lack of standardized validation + no durable failure reason surfaced to operators
3) “Success without manual touch” is below target (Dedicated 62%). Each manual touch adds queueing delays and increases variance.
4) We need an authoritative readiness state (Allocated/Provisioning/Validating/Ready/Quarantined) and per-step telemetry to make this measurable.

Proposed baseline targets for sprint (strawman; SRE to confirm)
- Dedicated pools: reduce P95 from ~212 min → <120 min (us-east A100 as pilot).
- Increase “success w/o manual touch” from 62% → 80% for pilot bucket.
- Cut reimage rate from 18% → <10% via golden image versioning + validation gates.

Change log
- 2025-09-29: Initial draft from FleetOps allocation logs + sampled kubelet joins.
- 2025-10-03: Added region x GPU breakdown; incorporated eu-central data.
- 2025-10-07: Added step-level sampled breakdown and ranked delay contributors.
